tables.heading_context: ## Build vs. Buy vs. Fine-Tune vs. RAG — Architecture Decision Tree
rows: Internal tool, small team, fast iteration
Cheapest path to value; don't optimize prematurely
Compliance posture, billing consolidation, existing agreements
GPT-4o-mini fine-tuned beats Sonnet at 1/20th the cost for narrow tasks
Don't fine-tune for knowledge freshness — RAG handles it
Managed APIs add 50-200ms network + queue latency
Compare instruction following, tool use, long-context behavior, evals, latency, and cost.
Public benchmarks are weaker than workload-specific evals.
Test reasoning trace quality, verifier pass rate, hallucination under pressure, and step budget.
"Reasoning model" does not remove the need for independent checking.
Measure accuracy/cost curve on classification, extraction, routing, and failure escalation.
Cheap models are good only if errors are bounded and detectable.
Evaluate retrieval quality, chunking, grounding, citation behavior, access control, and answer abstention.
Model choice cannot rescue a bad retrieval/indexing layer.
Test repo-specific edits, tool use, test repair, security reasoning, and diff quality.
General coding scores may not predict behavior in your codebase.
Check OCR, layout, tables, figures, grounding, and extraction schema reliability.
Vision models can read layout while still inventing relationships.
Compare open weights, hardware, quantization, ops burden, update cadence, and data boundary.
Self-hosting shifts risk from data residency to platform operations.
Test recall, positional bias, summarization drift, and retrieval augmentation.
A huge context window is not the same as reliable reasoning over all tokens.
Separate recognition/generation quality, control, latency, safety, rights, and downstream workflow.
Media models need product guardrails beyond model selection.
Check whether behavior, domain language, cost, or retrieval geometry is the real bottleneck.
Fine-tuning is not a substitute for good prompts, evals, or data cleaning.
